model.name: Payment
model.purpose: A format-neutral record of a transfer of a monetary claim from a payer toward a payee that may discharge or change a monetary obligation, capturing parties, amount, method, rail, authorization and settlement state without inlining money-as-instrument, invoices or accounting postings.
model.scope_statement: In scope is the payment as an evented transfer: identity and scheme classification; payer, payee and agent chain; account or proxy references; instructed and settled amounts and charges; payment order, authentication, mandate and request-to-pay; clearing, netting, settlement finality and value timing; status, returns, recalls, refunds and chargebacks; travel-rule and remittance data that accompany the transfer; screening outcomes for this transfer; inquiry, receipts, provenance, access and retention. The model covers credit transfers, direct debits, card, e-money, cheque and cash methods as transfer classifications, instant and deferred rails, domestic and cross-border chains, and linked exchange-of-value conditions on the payment leg. A payment may exist with no recorded underlying commercial claim. JSON, XML, YAML, ISO 20022 syntax, SWIFT MT, ISO 8583, ACH NACHA files, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections. Semantic identity is the transfer, its parties, amounts, method, rail and settlement state, independent of message syntax or store.
in_scope: Identity and scheme classification of the transfer
Instructed and settled amounts and charges
Payment order, authentication, mandate and request-to-pay
Clearing, netting, settlement finality and value timing
Status, returns, recalls, refunds and chargebacks
Travel-rule and remittance data that accompany the transfer
Inquiry, receipts, provenance, access and retention
Credit transfers, direct debits, card, e-money, cheque and cash methods as transfer classifications
Instant and deferred rails, domestic and cross-border chains
Linked exchange-of-value conditions on the payment leg
Payments with no recorded underlying commercial claim
out_of_scope: Currency catalogue, instrument forms, issuance and redemption, account-as-holding and balance-as-stock (sibling monetary-instrument model WM-ECO-004).
Invoice or bill as the commercial claim being settled (WM-ECO-008).
Accounting journal entries, ledgers and postings produced from a payment (WM-ECO-016).
Credit, loan or debt instruments themselves; only their servicing transfers appear here.
Person and organization master data; parties are referenced, not inlined.
Agreements and contracts as obligation sources; a payment may reference them.
FX rate catalogues as market data; a payment may snapshot a conversion used.
Sanctions, PEP and AML watchlists as datasets; only this payment's screening decision is in scope.

Card-scheme operating regulations, ISO 8583 bit maps, national faster-payment rulebooks (FedNow, PIX, UPI, FPS) and CBDC programmability beyond CPMI stablecoin-arrangement guidance, except as alignment or recorded gaps.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-ECO-004 monetary instrument (currency, instrument form, accounts as holdings)
boundary_notes.distinction: Currency catalogue, instrument forms, issuance, redemption and balances stay in the sibling model; a payment carries only amount snapshots and currency or instrument references.
The invoice is the claim; a payment may reference it through remittance information or a creditor reference without inlining it.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-ECO-016 financial transaction postings and ledgers
boundary_notes.distinction: Journal entries produced from a payment are accounting traces, not a second payment.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Person and organization master data models
boundary_notes.distinction: Parties are referenced by identity keys; only the travel-rule fields that must accompany the transfer are recorded here, not KYC attributes or party masters.
Obligation sources remain in their own models; a payment records optional discharge links and servicing transfers only.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Sanctions, PEP and AML watchlists and FX market-rate data
boundary_notes.distinction: List and rate catalogues are datasets elsewhere; only this payment's screening decision and the conversion snapshot applied to it are in scope.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Card-scheme operating regulations, ISO 8583 and national faster-payment rulebooks
boundary_notes.distinction: Scheme-specific field maps and national rulebooks are recorded as alignment targets or gaps, not modelled here.

bundles.name: Identity and classification
bundles.description: Identify a payment as a distinct transfer and classify instrument, scheme, direction and domestic or cross-border character without treating message syntax as identity.
bundles.rationale: Identity and classification sit first because every later fact hangs off a stable transfer identity, and because the message that carried the transfer must not be mistaken for that identity.

layers.name: Identifiers and correlation
layers.description: Record master-system, scheme, end-to-end and instruction identifiers so a transfer can be recognized across customer, PSP and rail projections.

findings.name: Master-system and scheme identifiers
findings.description: A payment is identified first by the identifier assigned in the master system of record (account-servicing PSP or settlement system), then by governed scheme identifiers that travel with the transfer. ISO 20022 payment initiation and clearing messages distinguish EndToEndIdentification, PaymentInformationIdentification, InstructionIdentification, TransactionIdentification and, for cross-border chains, a unique end-to-end transaction reference. CPMI harmonised data requirements treat consistent identification as a cross-border interoperability requirement. A calendar date is not an identifier.

layers.name: Instrument, scheme and direction
layers.description: Classify how the transfer is initiated and which scheme or instrument family it belongs to, independently of the monetary instrument stock.

findings.name: Payment instrument class and initiation direction
findings.description: CPMI statistics treat payment instruments as credit transfers, direct debits, card payments, e-money payments and cheques. A credit transfer is a payment order, or sequence of orders, made to place funds at the disposal of the payee, with both the order and the funds moving from the payer's institution to the payee's institution. A direct debit is a preauthorised debit of the payer's account initiated by the payee. PSD2 defines a payment transaction as an act, initiated by the payer or on his behalf or by the payee, of placing, transferring or withdrawing funds, irrespective of any underlying obligations. Instant credit transfer is a credit transfer executed immediately, 24 hours a day on any calendar day. Cash and card remain instrument classes even when detailed till or scheme-clearing rules live elsewhere.

bundles.name: Parties, agents and account references
bundles.description: Record who pays, who is paid, ultimate parties and the PSP or bank chain, using identity references rather than inlined person or organization masters.
bundles.rationale: Party and agent facts are grouped so that competing role vocabularies and the routing references that depend on them stay together, while party master data remains in sibling models.

layers.name: Payer, payee and ultimate parties
layers.description: Bind the economic payer and payee and any ultimate debtor or creditor without duplicating party master models.

findings.name: Payer, payee and ultimate party roles
findings.description: PSD2 defines the payer as the natural or legal person who holds a payment account and allows a payment order from that account, or who gives a payment order where there is no payment account, and the payee as the intended recipient of the funds. UCC Article 4A names originator, beneficiary, originator's bank, beneficiary's bank and intermediary bank, and treats a funds transfer as the series of transactions beginning with the originator's payment order and completed by acceptance by the beneficiary's bank. ISO 20022 additionally carries ultimate debtor and ultimate creditor when the account holder is not the economic party. Party location (address, country, town) is travel-rule and TFR data, not a geographic 'payment location' in the GIS sense.

data_elements.name: payee_party_ref

Is the account holder acting on behalf of an ultimate debtor or creditor, and which sibling party records identify those ultimate parties?
What country and structured address or town were supplied for payer and payee for travel-rule, TFR or scheme address rules, and is that data verified?

layers.name: Agents, account references and proxies
layers.description: Record the instructed agent chain and the account, IBAN, unique identifier or alias used to route funds.

findings.name: Agent and intermediary chain
findings.description: ISO 20022 pain and pacs messages carry debtor agent, creditor agent, instructing agent, instructed agent and intermediary agents. UCC 4A requires a receiving bank executing a payment order to follow the sender's instructions concerning any intermediary bank or funds-transfer system. FATF Recommendation 16 revisions clarify that the payment chain starts with the financial institution that receives an instruction from the customer and that information responsibilities must remain assigned along that chain. Correspondent cover (FI credit transfer used as cover) is a related but distinct settlement instruction, not a second customer payment.

Is settlement serial through correspondent accounts or does a separate cover instruction exist, and which payment record is the cover?
Which agent is currently instructed to execute or settle, and under which scheme participation or license does it act?

findings.name: Account, unique identifier and proxy references
findings.description: PSD2 uses a unique identifier specified by the PSP to identify unambiguously another payment service user or that user's payment account. ISO 20022 and EPC SCT carry IBAN or other account identification and, in the 2025 SCT rulebook, alias and proxy definitions. Account containers and balances as holdings belong to the monetary-instrument sibling; this model stores only the reference used to debit or credit. Name-versus-number mismatch is an execution rule (UCC 4A), not a reason to inline account masters.

bundles.name: Amount, charges, method and rail
bundles.description: Capture how much value is instructed and settled, who bears charges, and which payment system carries the transfer, while referencing currency and instrument rather than defining money.
bundles.rationale: Amount, charges, method and rail belong together because what the payee actually receives can only be reconciled when instructed value, deductions and the carrying system are read as one surface, without redefining money.

layers.name: Instructed value and charges
layers.description: Record instructed, equivalent and settled amounts, currency references, FX snapshot and charge bearer.

findings.name: Instructed, equivalent and settled amounts
findings.description: A CPMI payment is the payer's transfer of a monetary claim on a party acceptable to the payee, typically cash or deposit balances. ISO 20022 credit-transfer messages separate instructed amount, equivalent amount and interbank settlement amount, each with a currency code that must reference the monetary-unit sibling rather than copy a currency catalogue. Partial settlement and remaining amount are operational facts on some rails. FX conversion used on this payment is a snapshot bound to the transfer, not a market-rate object.

findings.description: ISO 20022 ChargeBearer distinguishes whether charges are borne by the debtor, creditor or shared. CPMI cross-border data requirements include a consistent minimum set of data end to end, which in market practice includes charge information needed to reconcile what the payee receives. Fees may be separate related payments; they must not silently mutate the instructed amount after settlement.

layers.name: Rail, clearing method and exchange of value
layers.description: Identify the payment system, clearing versus settlement method, and any PvP or DvP condition on this payment leg.

findings.name: Rail, clearing and settlement method
findings.description: A payment system is a set of instruments, procedures and rules for the transfer of funds among participants, including the operator. Clearing is transmitting, reconciling and in some cases confirming transactions prior to settlement, potentially including netting; the term is sometimes used imprecisely to cover settlement. Settlement is the discharge of an obligation in accordance with the underlying contract. Systems may be RTGS, deferred net settlement or hybrid. PFMI Principle 9 prefers central-bank money for FMI money settlements where practical. PFMI Principle 22 requires internationally accepted communication procedures and standards.

data_elements.name: payment_system_operator_ref

data_elements.name: clearing_method

data_elements.name: clearing_system_ref

Which scheme rulebook, FMI participation agreement and message standard bind this payment to the rail?

findings.name: Exchange-of-value linkage
findings.description: PFMI Principle 12 requires that if an FMI settles two linked obligations, it eliminate principal risk by conditioning final settlement of one upon final settlement of the other. A PvP system ensures that the final payment of one currency occurs if and only if the final payment of the other occurs. DvP model 1 settles securities and funds gross, obligation by obligation, with final transfer of securities if and only if final transfer of funds occurs. This model records the payment leg and the linkage condition; the securities or FX trade objects remain in sibling models.

data_elements.name: principal_risk_eliminated

findings.name: Payment order as instruction
findings.description: UCC § 4A-103 defines a payment order as an instruction of a sender to a receiving bank to pay, or cause another bank to pay, a fixed or determinable amount of money to a beneficiary, without a condition to payment other than time of payment; the order is issued when sent to the receiving bank. PSD2 defines a payment order as an instruction by a payer or payee to its PSP requesting execution of a payment transaction, and a payment instrument as a personalised device or set of procedures used to initiate a payment order. ISO 20022 pain.001 is the customer credit-transfer initiation; pain.008 is customer direct-debit initiation. A batch file may contain many payment orders; each credit transfer in a bulk is a separate payment.

UCC § 4A-202 treats a payment order as the authorized order of the sender, or as effective if accepted in good faith in compliance with a commercially reasonable security procedure. Consent and SCA evidence are payment-specific facts; identity proofing of the person belongs to the person model.

findings.name: Mandate and request-to-pay

Creditor payment activation / request-to-pay (pain.013/pain.014) asks the payer to initiate a credit transfer rather than pulling funds. EPC SCT rulebooks additionally specify recall initiation and status-update handling, which are exception processes on an already initiated credit transfer, not a mandate. A mandate is not the invoice and not the payment.

findings.name: Acceptance, finality and discharge
findings.description: PFMI Principle 8 requires an FMI to provide clear and certain final settlement at least by the end of the value date, and where necessary or preferable, intraday or in real time. CPMI defines final settlement as the irrevocable and unconditional transfer of an asset or discharge of an obligation; it is a legally defined moment. Acceptance for settlement is the processing stage at which a payment has passed risk-management tests and can be settled under the system's rules. Under UCC § 4A-209 a receiving bank other than the beneficiary's bank accepts by executing; the beneficiary's bank accepts by paying, notifying, receiving payment, or at a defined funds-transfer business-day event. UCC § 4A-406 treats the originator as paying the beneficiary when the beneficiary's bank accepts, and that payment discharges an underlying obligation unless the contract forbade that means and specified loss conditions apply. Settlement Finality Directive protection of designated systems is a regional legal overlay, not a global fact.

findings.name: Execution clocks, value date and instant SLA

EPC SCT Inst scheme rules add tighter originator-PSP response expectations. Value date is a business date, not an identifier. Event time and ingestion time must be stored separately when they differ.

EPC SCT rulebooks specify recall initiation, status-update requests and R-transaction reason codes. Unwinding in some net systems recalculates obligations if a participant fails to settle; such unwinds are system-level exceptions, not silent edits of a settled customer payment. Status codes are scheme-aligned enumerations projected from ISO 20022 external codes.

findings.name: Travel-rule payload and screening
findings.description: FATF Recommendation 16 requires countries to ensure that financial institutions include required and accurate originator information and required beneficiary information on wire payments or value transfers and related messages. The June 2025 update standardises responsibilities in the payment chain, starting with the institution that receives the customer instruction, and applies enhanced data for peer-to-peer cross-border payments above USD/EUR 1,000 (name, address, date of birth among other fields). The EU Transfer of Funds rules require the payer's PSP to accompany transfers with payer and payee name and account number (or unique transaction identifier where no account), plus specified identity details, and to verify payer information before execution; the payee's PSP must detect missing data and may execute, reject or suspend. Screening against restrictive measures is a pre-execution control; list contents are out of scope. Crypto-asset transfers are covered by the TFR recast; detailed on-chain semantics remain a gap.

findings.name: Provenance, stewardship and retention
findings.description: Each payment record has a steward: typically the account-servicing PSP for customer orders and the settlement-system operator for rail settlement facts. PSD2 evidential duties imply retention of authorization and execution evidence. EU transfer-of-funds rules require policies, procedures and controls and imply multi-year retention aligned to AML law; exact retention periods are jurisdictional. Settled facts are not silently overwritten; returns and corrections are related events. Default access is least-privilege to parties of the payment and their PSPs; competent authorities and scheme operators get scoped exceptions with audit. AGENTS.md remains the bootstrap contract regardless of MongoDB, files or MCP storage.

From which source message or API assertion was this fact ingested, what hash or copy identifies that source, and what are event time versus ingestion time?
Until when must the payment and its authorization evidence be retained, is a legal hold in force, and which audit log records each read, exception access or deletion event?

functions.name: Initiate credit transfer
functions.description: Accept a payer or PISP instruction to place funds at the payee's disposal, validate unique identifiers, attach travel-rule data and create a payment order without settling it.
inputs: Originator and beneficiary information required to travel
outputs: Payment order record carrying master-system and end-to-end identifiers
preconditions: The sender is entitled to instruct the debtor agent
The payee unique identifier is present and validated
effects: A payment order exists in an initiated, unsettled state
Travel-rule data is attached to the order

functions.name: Initiate direct debit
functions.description: Create a payee-initiated debit against a valid mandate, generating a distinct payment order per occurrence.
inputs: Payee instruction with amount and payer account identifier
outputs: A distinct payment order for this direct-debit occurrence
preconditions: A mandate exists, is in force and covers this creditor, account and amount
effects: A pull payment order exists referencing the mandate
The mandate sequence advances for the next occurrence

functions.name: Authenticate and authorize
functions.description: Apply the agreed security procedure or SCA, record consent and produce authorization evidence before execution.
inputs: User credentials or agreed security procedure
Consent record where a third-party provider initiates
preconditions: A payment order exists that has not yet been executed
effects: Authorization evidence is recorded and retained with the payment
Execution may proceed, or the order is refused

functions.name: Verify payee
functions.description: Match the instructed unique identifier to the payee name via scheme directory and record match, close-match or mismatch before the payer confirms execution.
outputs: Match, close-match or mismatch result with the time of the check
preconditions: The payer has not yet confirmed the order for execution
effects: The verification result is recorded on the payment
A payer decision to proceed after a non-match is recorded as an exception

functions.name: Screen and enrich travel-rule data
functions.description: Complete originator and beneficiary information, verify required fields, screen restrictive measures and block, freeze or release the order.
inputs: Applicable threshold and the jurisdictions in the chain
outputs: Completeness assessment of the required payload
preconditions: The payment order exists and has not yet been sent to the rail
effects: The order is released, rejected, suspended or the funds frozen
The screening decision and any hit reference are recorded

functions.name: Clear and settle
functions.description: Route the instruction through the selected rail, apply netting or RTGS rules, and record acceptance and legally defined final settlement.
outputs: Acceptance record and, on completion, a legally defined final settlement moment
preconditions: The instruction has passed the system's risk-management tests
effects: Settlement obligations are discharged under the system's rules
Final settlement indicator and finality time become immutable once recorded

functions.name: Report status
functions.description: Emit customer and FI status reports and debit/credit advice for a payment without creating a new transfer.
outputs: Customer or interbank status report, or debit/credit advice
preconditions: The reporting party is an agent or party of the payment
effects: A status projection is emitted without creating a second payment
Status event time and observation time are both recorded

functions.name: Request recall or return
functions.description: Open a cancellation, recall or post-settlement return with a reason code, producing a related payment or investigation case rather than mutating the original.
outputs: Cancellation, recall or return case with a reason code
Related return payment where funds move back
preconditions: The applicable scheme or statutory window for the exception is still open
effects: A related event or payment is created
The original payment record is not mutated

functions.name: Refund unauthorized or defective payment
functions.description: Restore the payer's account when authorization or execution fails statutory tests, allocating liability between ASPSP and PISP.
inputs: Roles of account-servicing PSP and PISP
outputs: Refund transfer restoring the payer's account
preconditions: The claim was filed within the statutory or scheme window
effects: The debited account is restored
Liability is allocated between the account-servicing PSP and the PISP

functions.name: Inquire payment
functions.description: Allow an entitled party to retrieve lifecycle status, amounts and limited party data under least-privilege access.
inputs: Payment identifier or scheme correlation identifier
outputs: Lifecycle status, amounts and the party data the requester is entitled to see
preconditions: The requester is a party or agent of the payment, the rail operator for its own rail, or an authority with a recorded legal basis
effects: An audited read of non-aggregated payment data is recorded
No new transfer is created

composition.purpose: A payment references the monetary unit or instrument being transferred; it does not define currency, instrument form, issuance or holdings.
An invoice may be settled by one or more payments via remittance or creditor reference; the invoice remains the commercial claim.
A payment produces one or more financial transactions or postings on ledgers; those postings are accounting traces, not a second payment.
Natural-person payers, payees and ultimate parties are referenced by identity keys; KYC attributes live on the person model.
PSPs, FMI operators, corporate payers and payees and LEI-identified entities are referenced, not inlined.
A payment may discharge or change an obligation arising under an agreement; PSD2 still treats the transfer as existing irrespective of underlying obligations.
Interest, principal and fee servicing appear here as payments; the credit claim itself remains on the credit-debt model.
Field equivalences with ISO 20022 pain, pacs and camt payment semantics; alignment is not a claim that every instance is scheme-conformant.
Settlement-finality, money-settlement and exchange-of-value principles apply when the rail is an FMI; not every retail payment system is a designated FMI.
EEA payment-service definitions, authorization, PISP liability and execution clocks align when an EEA PSP is in the chain.
US wholesale credit-transfer acceptance and discharge rules align for funds transfers governed by UCC Article 4A, not for all consumer or ACH products.
Originator and beneficiary information that accompanies a cross-border value transfer aligns to FATF Recommendation 16; thresholds and field lists remain jurisdictional.
Euro credit transfers among SCT scheme participants align to the EPC SCT rulebook for recalls, aliases and R-transactions.

owner_package_requirements: The owning package publishes AGENTS.md at its root with Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before any CRUD is attempted.
Every payment record carries a named steward: the account-servicing PSP for customer orders, the settlement-system operator for rail settlement facts.
The package records its retention, legal-hold and audit configuration before ingesting settled payment facts.
The package declares which legal regime governs revocability and finality for each rail it carries.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Identifiers are namespaced by the system that assigned them: EndToEndIdentification, InstructionIdentification and TransactionIdentification are unique only inside their scheme and agent pair, so they are stored with the assigning system's namespace rather than as bare strings. A UUID or ULID is minted in the Dimension namespace only when no master-system or governed global identifier exists.
registry_links: Sibling references: WM-ECO-004 monetary instrument, WM-ECO-008 invoice, WM-ECO-016 financial transaction postings
Alignment targets: ISO 20022 payment message definitions, PFMI, PSD2, UCC Article 4A, EPC SCT rulebook, FATF Recommendation 16

canonicalization_rules: Canonical identity is the master-system payment identifier plus its assigning system; message identification is never used as the payment's identity.
Timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset; value date and requested execution date stay business dates and are never used as identifiers.
Amounts are canonicalised as an amount plus a currency reference to the sibling monetary-unit model, never as a formatted string carrying its own currency catalogue.
Status and reason values are canonicalised to the code list that issued them and recorded with that list's name, rather than merged into one vocabulary.
patch_rules: Settled payment facts are append-mostly: returns, recalls, refunds, chargebacks and corrections are new related events that reference the original master-system identifier.
Fields on a non-final order may be repaired only under the scheme's repair rules and only with an audit trail naming actor, basis and event time.
Final settlement indicator, finality time and discharged-obligation links are immutable once recorded; any later change is expressed through a related exception payment.
A patch never silently overwrites amount, parties or finality.
compatibility_rules: Alignment with ISO 20022, PFMI, PSD2, UCC Article 4A, EPC SCT and FATF Recommendation 16 is field equivalence, not a claim of conformance for every instance.
New scheme code values are added as additional enumerated values carrying their issuing list; existing values are not redefined.
Consumers must tolerate absent optional fields, because required travel-rule and remittance payloads differ by jurisdiction, threshold and rail.
A projection into a message syntax may drop fields only where the scheme allows it; truncation by an intermediary is recorded rather than treated as the new truth.

identity_priority: governed global identifier or IRI such as a scheme UETR or namespaced EndToEndId
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Timestamps use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. Record event time (when the payment event occurred at the PSP or rail) separately from observation or ingestion time (when this Dimension recorded the fact) whenever those differ. Value date and requested execution date are business dates, not identifiers.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts — message instances, batches, mandates and their amendments — keep the series value assigned by the issuing system (message identification, payment information or batch identifier, mandate identifier with amendment sequence). A series value is stored with its issuer and scope, is never reused for a different artifact, and is never renumbered after issue.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Settled payment facts are append-mostly. Returns, recalls, refunds, chargebacks and corrections are new related events that reference the original master-system identifier; silent overwrite of amount, parties or finality is forbidden. Source-message hash or equivalent integrity stamp is stored with each ingested assertion.

policies: Do not execute a cross-border payment until travel-rule originator and beneficiary information required for the applicable threshold is complete and payer data has been verified.
Authorization evidence and dual-control or SCA results must be retained with the payment; execution without recorded authorization is an exception event, not a normal create.
Least-privilege access: only parties to the payment, their PSPs, the rail operator for its own rail, and competent authorities with a recorded legal basis may read non-aggregated payment data.
Deletion of a settled payment is prohibited while a retention or legal hold applies; any later erasure or anonymisation emits an auditable deletion event that preserves the master-system identifier.

read: A payer, payee or their PSP may read the payment fields they are party to.
A PISP may read status of payments it initiated, within consent scope.
A settlement-rail operator may read payments on its rail for operations, finality and statistics.
A competent authority may read with a recorded legal basis.
Aggregated rail volumes without party identification may be read more widely.
create: A payer or authorized PISP creates a credit-transfer payment order at the debtor agent.
A payee or payee PSP creates a direct-debit order only against a valid mandate.
A rail or instructed agent creates FI-to-FI child instructions that reference the originator payment.
The Dimension may create a UUID or ULID only when no master-system identifier yet exists.
update: Status, screening, verification-of-payee and advice fields may be updated as new events.
Party or amount fields on a non-final order may be repaired only under scheme repair rules with an audit trail.
Final settlement indicator, final_at and discharged-obligation links become immutable once finality is recorded, except via related exception payments.
delete: Hard delete of a settled or legally retained payment is denied.
After the retention period and with no legal hold, personal data may be erased or anonymised while keeping non-identifying operational statistics.
Every deletion or anonymisation writes a deletion event with actor, legal basis and RFC 3339 event time.

roles.name: payer-payment-service-user
responsibilities: Supply unique identifiers and travel-rule data

roles.name: payee
responsibilities: Initiate direct debits only under mandate
Accept or refuse a credit after notice where scheme allows

roles.name: account-servicing-psp
responsibilities: Report status to users and to the next agent

roles.name: settlement-rail-operator
responsibilities: Declare the legally defined finality moment
Operate participant access and default procedures
Publish operating calendar and SLA metrics without party identification

roles.name: payment-initiation-service-provider
responsibilities: Initiate payments with user consent without holding funds when acting only as PISP
Prove authorization and technical integrity within its sphere
Receive status needed to confirm initiation to the payee

roles.name: compliance-officer
responsibilities: Decide freeze, reject or release on screening hits
Preserve AML evidence for the retention period

access.default_rule: Deny all non-aggregated payment data except to recorded parties of the payment, their account-servicing PSPs, and the rail operator for payments on its own rail.
exceptions: Competent authorities with a recorded statutory basis may read specified findings or artifacts.
Scheme operators may read R-transaction and recall fields required to operate the scheme.
A PISP reads only payments it initiated, within consent scope and time.
Public or research consumers may receive rail-level aggregates with no party, account or unique-identifier data.
audit_requirements: Record actor, role, scope, purpose and RFC 3339 event time for every read of non-aggregated payment data.
Record every authorization, screening decision, repair, recall, refund and deletion event with source-message hash.
Make audit logs available to the steward and to competent authorities; do not use audit logs as a shadow payment ledger.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md Name and Type first to identify this Dimension
Read Specification URL for the payment meta-model
Read Storage type URL and Interface URL before any CRUD
Read Processes URL for initiation, settlement, inquiry and exception processes

coverage.claim: This structure is a defensible, format-neutral operating surface for Payment as a transfer with parties, amount, method and settlement state, grounded in ISO 20022 payment messages, the CPMI glossary and PFMI, PSD2 and EU instant-transfer and transfer-of-funds rules, UCC Article 4A, EPC SCT and FATF Recommendation 16. It does not claim universal completeness across every retail scheme, card network, cheque law, CBDC or national faster-payment rulebook.

checklist.notes: Master-system identifier, ISO 20022 end-to-end/instruction/transaction identifiers and optional Dimension UUID/ULID; dates excluded as identifiers.
Order issuance, acceptance, status codes, finality, returns, recalls, refunds and chargebacks as related events.
Payer/payee/ultimate parties, agent chain, account references, invoice/agreement/money/posting links.
Time of receipt, value date, execution date, instant SLA, settlement lag; RFC 3339 event time versus ingestion time.
Identifier assignment, source-message hash/URI, status reporter, ingestion versus event time.
Stewardship split between holder/ASPSP and rail operator; charge bearer as economic ownership of fees.
SCA/security procedure, mandate bounds, travel-rule completeness, verification of payee, funds and scheme checks before execution.
Least-privilege party/PSP/rail access, PISP consent scope, authority exceptions and audit of reads.
AML/TFR-aligned retention, legal hold, append-mostly settled facts, auditable erasure after retention.
ISO 20022 alignment, CPMI minimum cross-border data set, PFMI communication standards, IBAN/proxy identifiers; national rails marked as gaps where not fetched.
PFMI Principle 8, CPMI final settlement definition, UCC acceptance/discharge; SFD designated-system protection treated as regional.
FATF R.16 June 2025 update and EU TFR accompanying information; crypto-asset on-chain detail remains a gap.
ISO 20022 returns/cancellations, EPC R-transactions, PSD2 unauthorized refunds; card chargeback catalogues not primary-fetched.

known_omissions: Visa, Mastercard and other card-scheme chargeback operating regulations and ISO 8583 authorization/clearing field maps were not retrieved as primary texts.
National instant systems (FedNow, PIX, UPI, Faster Payments, PromptPay and others) are not modelled beyond EU instant SCT and generic CPMI fast-payment timing.
Cheque presentment law and cash-till operations are classified as instrument classes only.
CBDC, tokenised deposits and programmable escrow remain emerging; only CPMI-IOSCO stablecoin-arrangement PFMI guidance is acknowledged, not fetched in full.
Correspondent banking cover-method edge cases and in-house multilaterally nested nostro chains are sketched, not exhausted.
W3C Payment Request API and merchant checkout objects are out of this transfer model.
Exact AML retention periods vary by jurisdiction and are not encoded as a single number.
Person/org KYC attributes, sanctions list content and FX market-rate histories are sibling concerns.
conflicts: Registry purpose says a payment discharges or changes a monetary obligation, while PSD2 defines a payment transaction irrespective of any underlying obligations. This model records optional discharge links and allows transfers with no recorded claim (gifts, cash-out, errors).

PSD2 makes a payment order irrevocable after time of receipt subject to listed exceptions, UCC 4A allows cancellation before acceptance by the beneficiary's bank, and EPC SCT permits post-settlement recall in limited cases. Lifecycle must store which legal regime governs.
UCC 4A-207 name-versus-account-number reliance can diverge from EU verification-of-payee match-before-pay.
ISO 20022 transaction status codes and EPC R-transaction reason codes overlap but are not identical vocabularies; treat as aligned enumerations, not one code list.
Instant 10-second statutory SLA (EU Regulation 260/2012 as amended) is stricter than PSD2 D+1 execution for ordinary credit transfers and may differ from EPC SCT Inst scheme timings.
ISO 20022 implementations remain inconsistent across jurisdictions; CPMI d218 exists because fragmentation undercuts the standard. Alignment is not conformance.
regional_assumptions: IBAN as the default unique identifier is an EEA/SEPA assumption; other regions use national account numbers plus routing codes.
UCC Article 4A governs US wholesale funds transfers and Fedwire-like credit transfers, not all US consumer ACH products (NACHA).
Settlement Finality Directive protection applies to designated systems in the EEA and equivalent regimes, not globally.
FATF R.16 enhanced data at USD/EUR 1,000 is a FATF threshold; local implementation may differ.
Instant 24/7/365 with 10-second availability is an EU instant-credit-transfer rule, not a universal rail property.
Address structured/hybrid/unstructured transition dates in EPC SCT (unstructured address no longer permitted from 15 November 2026 per 2025 rulebook v1.1) are SEPA-scheme specific.
adversarial_checks: Money-versus-transfer: currency catalogue, cash/deposit stock, issuance and balances were excluded and pointed at WM-ECO-004; only amount snapshots and instrument references remain here.
Invoice and ledger duplication: invoices stay WM-ECO-008 via remittance references; journal postings stay WM-ECO-016 via COMPOSE, not as extra payments.
Conformance claim avoided: ISO 20022, PFMI, PSD2, UCC 4A, FATF and EPC are recorded as ALIGN or regime-conditional, never as universal conformance.

Rare lifecycles included with primary support (instant timeout, cover method, mandate, request-to-pay, recall after settlement, unauthorized refund) and marked as gaps where primary text was not fetched (card chargeback codes, CBDC programmes).
